title: Third Hom-colimit bijection from a triangle retraction
statement: In Situation 05S8 [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], let F:C -> D be exact and T a distinguished triangle [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Supply left-derived values LX and LY for its first two vertices, with cones uX and uY and their retraction/common-stage certificates [def-pc-essentially-constant-pro-diagram]. Fix a distinguished triangle (LX,LY,K,lf,b,c). Let U be distinguished and sigma:U -> T a triangle morphism whose three components belong to S. Let rho:F(U) -> (LX,LY,K,lf,b,c) be a triangle morphism such that the uX cone leg at sigma1 followed by rho1 is the identity of LX, and the uY cone leg at sigma2 followed by rho2 is the identity of LY. Then for every W in D, the map Hom(K,W) -> colim over (S/T.obj3)^op of Hom(F(Zprime),W), sending phi to the class of rho3 followed by phi at the denominator sigma3, is bijective. This statement makes no assertion about a third derived value or a distinguished triangle on a supplied third value.

source.place: Lemma 05SC, LF clause, dual of the RF proof

proof.text: Use the cofiltered category I of incoming distinguished denominator triangles over T, with initial vertex projections p1, p2, p3. Regard sigma:U -> T as its object i0. Restrict the supplied cones uX and uY along p1 and p2. Initial essential-constancy restriction supplies essential constancy of the restricted diagrams and the common-stage certificates for those particular restricted cones. No denominator postcomposition functor is needed.

Apply the canonical Hom-colimit bijection to each restricted cone. The representative map induced at i0 by rho.hom1 or rho.hom2 is its inverse: the composite with the canonical bijection is precomposition with uX(i0) followed by rho.hom1, or uY(i0) followed by rho.hom2, hence the identity by the supplied retraction identities. Injectivity of the canonical bijection gives surjectivity of the representative map, and its left inverse gives injectivity. This is the proved private helper retraction_homColimit_bijective.

Form the functor G:I -> Triangle(D) by taking the F-image of each distinguished source triangle. The functor F is triangulated, so every value is distinguished. Apply triangulated_hom_colimit_comparison to G, the fixed distinguished triangle (LX,LY,K), i0 and rho, using the two all-W bijections just proved. This gives the third-vertex Hom-colimit bijection over I opposite.

The third projection p3 is initial, so p3.op is final. Compose the third comparison with Mathlib Functor.bijective_colimitTypePrecomp. Its representative formula sends the object i0 exactly to the denominator sigma.hom3 and rho.hom3 followed by phi to the same morphism, giving the function of the original theorem definitionally.

proof_origin.place: Lemma 05SC LF dual: existing five-term comparison; use the denominator-triangle category over T directly rather than postcomposing denominators over U

theorem leftDerived_triangle_retraction_homColimit
    {C : Type u} {D : Type uD} [Category.{v} C] [Category.{vD} D]
    [HasZeroObject C] [HasShift C ℤ] [Preadditive C]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor C n).Additive] [Pretriangulated C]
    [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated C]
    [HasZeroObject D] [HasShift D ℤ] [Preadditive D]
    [∀ n : ℤ, (shiftFunctor D n).Additive] [Pretriangulated D]
    [CategoryTheory.IsTriangulated D]
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.CommShift ℤ] [F.IsTriangulated]
    (S : MorphismProperty C)
    (hS : S.IsSaturatedTriangulatedMultiplicativeSystem)
    (T : Triangle C) (hT : T ∈ distTriang C)
    (LX LY : D)
    (hX : F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedValue S hS T.obj₁ LX)
    (hY : F.IsTriangulatedLeftDerivedValue S hS T.obj₂ LY)
    (uX : (Functor.const (S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁)).obj LX ⟶
      MorphismProperty.Over.forget S ⊤ T.obj₁ ⋙ Over.forget T.obj₁ ⋙ F)
    (uY : (Functor.const (S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂)).obj LY ⟶
      MorphismProperty.Over.forget S ⊤ T.obj₂ ⋙ Over.forget T.obj₂ ⋙ F)
    (huX : ∃ s₀ : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁, ∃ r : F.obj s₀.left ⟶ LX,
      uX.app s₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 LX ∧
        ∀ s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁, ∃ t : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₁,
          ∃ a : t ⟶ s₀, ∃ b : t ⟶ s,
            F.map b.left = F.map a.left ≫ r ≫ uX.app s)
    (huY : ∃ s₀ : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂, ∃ r : F.obj s₀.left ⟶ LY,
      uY.app s₀ ≫ r = 𝟙 LY ∧
        ∀ s : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂, ∃ t : S.Over ⊤ T.obj₂,
          ∃ a : t ⟶ s₀, ∃ b : t ⟶ s,
            F.map b.left = F.map a.left ≫ r ≫ uY.app s)
    (lf : LX ⟶ LY) (K : D) (b : LY ⟶ K)
    (c : K ⟶ (shiftFunctor D (1 : ℤ)).obj LX)
    (hK : Triangle.mk lf b c ∈ distTriang D)
    (U : Triangle C) (hU : U ∈ distTriang C) (sigma : U ⟶ T)
    (hsigma₁ : S sigma.hom₁) (hsigma₂ : S sigma.hom₂) (hsigma₃ : S sigma.hom₃)
    (rho : F.mapTriangle.obj U ⟶ Triangle.mk lf b c)
    (hretract₁ : uX.app (MorphismProperty.Over.mk ⊤ sigma.hom₁ hsigma₁) ≫
      rho.hom₁ = 𝟙 LX)
    (hretract₂ : uY.app (MorphismProperty.Over.mk ⊤ sigma.hom₂ hsigma₂) ≫
      rho.hom₂ = 𝟙 LY) :
    ∀ W : D, Function.Bijective (fun phi : K ⟶ W ↦
      ((MorphismProperty.Over.forget S ⊤ T.obj₃ ⋙ Over.forget T.obj₃ ⋙ F).op ⋙
        yoneda.obj W).ιColimitType
          (Opposite.op (MorphismProperty.Over.mk ⊤ sigma.hom₃ hsigma₃))
          (rho.hom₃ ≫ phi))
